script.title: ಹರಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಸಂಪತ್ತನ್ನೇ ಬೇಡ ಅಂದ ಯೋಧ ಕನಕ, ಕೇಳಿದ್ದೇನು 🙏
sentences: ಸಾಕ್ಷಾತ್ ಹರಿ ಕೊಡ್ತೀನಿ ಅಂದ ಸಂಪತ್ತನ್ನೇ ಕನಕದಾಸರು ಬೇಡ ಅಂದ್ರು.
ಕನಕ ಜಯಂತಿಯ ಕನಕದಾಸರು ಹಿಂದೆ ಬಂಕಾಪುರ ಕೋಟೆಯ ಯೋಧ ತಿಮ್ಮಪ್ಪ ನಾಯಕ.
ಕಥೆಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ, ಯುದ್ಧದಲ್ಲಿ ಗಾಯಗೊಂಡ ಅವರು ಹರಿನಾಮ ಜಪಿಸತೊಡಗಿದರು.
ಆಗ ಒಬ್ಬ ಭಿಕ್ಷುಕ ಬಂದು, ನೀನೇ ನನ್ನ ಕರೆದೆ ಅಂದ.
ಮೂರು ವರ ಕೊಡ್ತೀನಿ ಅಂದ ಹರಿ, ಮೊದಲು ಸಂಪತ್ತು ಬೇಕಾ ಅಂದರು.
ಕನಕ ಅದು ಬೇಡ ಅಂದು, ಗಾಯ ವಾಸಿ, ಕರೆದಾಗ ಬರೋದು, ನಿಜರೂಪ ದರ್ಶನ, ಇಷ್ಟೇ ಕೇಳಿದರು.
ಆ ರೂಪ ನೋಡಿ ಯೋಧನ ಕೆಲಸ ಬಿಟ್ಟು, ಸುಮಾರು 240 ಹಾಡು ಕಟ್ಟಿದರು.
ಹರಿಯೇ ಕರೆದಾಗ ಬರುವಾಗ, ಚಿನ್ನ ಯಾಕೆ ಬೇಕು?
script.description:
ಬಂಕಾಪುರದ ಯೋಧ ತಿಮ್ಮಪ್ಪ ನಾಯಕ ಕನಕದಾಸರಾದ ಕಥೆ.
ಹರಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಮೂರು ವರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅವರು ಕೇಳಿದ್ದೇನು.
claims_en: According to legend, Lord Hari offered Kanaka Dasa treasures and he refused.
Kanaka Dasa's birthday is celebrated in Karnataka as Kanakadasa Jayanthi.
Kanaka Dasa was earlier called Thimmappa Nayaka.
He was a warrior at the Bankapura fort.
He was injured in battle and took to chanting the name of Lord Hari.
A beggar appeared and said he was called by Kanaka.
Kanaka understood the beggar to be Lord Hari himself.
Lord Hari offered three wishes and first asked if Kanaka wanted treasures.
Kanaka refused and asked to be healed of his injuries, for Hari to appear whenever he called, and to see Hari's original form.
After seeing Hari's original form, Kanaka abandoned his profession as a soldier.
scenes: Extreme close-up of the young warrior Kanaka Dasa's face, eyes wide with awe and tears, refusing with a raised palm a glowing offer of gold, 16th-century Karnataka warrior turban, golden divine light on his face.
The young warrior Thimmappa Nayaka in 16th-century armour and turban standing on the stone ramparts of Bankapura fort, proud and restless expression, dusty afternoon light, wide shot.
The wounded warrior resting against a tree near a battlefield, bandaged arm, eyes closed, lips moving in quiet prayer to Hari, calm dusk light, medium shot, no blood.
A humble old beggar in simple cloth standing before the seated warrior, gentle knowing smile, the warrior looking up puzzled, village path at sunset, medium shot.
The warrior's face changing to astonishment as a soft blue divine glow surrounds the beggar, hands folding in reverence, twilight, close shot.
Lord Hari (Krishna) in traditional iconography, blue-skinned, crowned, gently offering a heap of gold and jewels to the kneeling warrior, serene smile, radiant light, medium shot.
The kneeling warrior shaking his head at the gold, hands folded, speaking earnestly to Lord Hari, his face humble and certain, warm divine light, medium shot.
Kanaka Dasa as a saint-poet in simple white clothes, holding a tambura, singing joyfully under a temple tree, villagers listening, warm morning light, wide shot.
Kanaka Dasa smiling peacefully with eyes closed, tambura in hand, faint image of Lord Krishna in the soft light behind him, gold coins left untouched on the ground, golden hour, medium close-up.
